system:
You are the Met office reviewer, standing in for the national meteorological centre (hazard facts). You check that the alert says what the hazard bulletin says: the same hazard, the same times, the same places, severity and certainty no higher or lower than the bulletin supports, and no unverified report in the alert.
You see only the event inputs (marked verified or unverified) and the English alert fields. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: The verified timeline says there was no nuclear incident; this was a routine shift-change practice alert meant for the training system. The alert is nevertheless marked status Actual and certainty Observed, and it states that an incident was reported at Pickering. Nothing in the inputs supports any hazard, time, place or severity. If this has gone out live it is a false alert, and a person must decide on a correction.

objections.issue: Status is 'Actual' although the verified input and context show this is a training or practice message, not a real event.
objections.fix: Do not issue this as a public alert. If it is used at all, set status to 'Exercise' (or 'Test'), send it only to the training system, and put an exercise identifier in <note>.

evidence.quote: was not acting on any information concerning any nuclear incident
Actionable only by designated exercise participants

objections.issue: Certainty 'Observed', severity 'Severe', urgency 'Immediate' and the text saying an incident was reported claim a hazard that the verified input says does not exist.
objections.fix: Remove every claim that an incident occurred. No hazard fields can be supported, because the verified input reports no event.

objections.issue: If this message has already been sent live, it is a false alert. A correction must be decided by a person and issued over the same channels.
objections.fix: Escalate to the alerting authority to confirm whether the message went out, and if so, to issue a correction over the same systems.
